values.goal: Call actual Wasm modules and distinguish linear memory·copying·numeric representation·initialization costs.
values.capstone: Validate array transformations in JS and actual Wasm, then decide whether to adopt Wasm using cold·warm·copy-inclusive end-to-end latency.

values.title: Modules and Linear Memory
values.prerequisites: Understand JavaScript·TypedArray and the basics of the chosen compiled language, and be able to read the inputs and outputs of the existing starting examples.
values.environment: The iframe preview is an experiment with WebAssembly.Memory and JS reference computations; do not present it as execution of an actual Wasm module. Practice with actual modules in a separate Node 22+ environment or a controlled local web project. Use kernel.wat·kernel.wasm·benchmark.mjs in the existing src/labs/webassembly-02·03 folders, and rebuild with the official wat2wasm tool when modifying WAT. Preserve CSP·isolation, and record measurements yourself.
values.concepts.0.title: Module boundary
values.concepts.0.explanation: Wasm calls exports of a compiled module. JS generally handles DOM manipulation.
values.concepts.1.title: Preview scope
values.concepts.1.explanation: The existing first example observes WebAssembly.Memory. It does not compile a module or accelerate computation.
values.outcomes.0: Learning outcome: explain the role of Module boundary. Input cases: [1,2,3] and an invalid file path.
values.outcomes.1: Deliverable: JS·Wasm sum 6 and a record of loading errors. Explain the rationale for handling Preview scope, linking it to the code.
values.steps.0: In day-1.mjs in a separate practice project, read the existing Memory example, then instantiate webassembly-02's kernel.wasm in a separate Node environment and call sum. Refer to the existing Unit 1·14·28 examples only as starting points.
values.steps.1: Input conditions: [1,2,3] and an invalid file path. Baseline: valid wasm. Run under the baseline conditions, then record observations and errors in notes/day-1.md.
values.steps.2: Variable: file path; changed value: missing file. Run again through the same input path. Deliverable to save: JS·Wasm sum 6 and a record of loading errors. Hypothesis to check: Normal results and loading failures are distinguished. Compare it with the actual results, and record whether they agree and why they differ.

values.criteria.1: The explanation of differences between the two conditions connects both concepts: Module boundary and Preview scope. For unexpected items, at least 1 cause or reason they remain unresolved is recorded.
values.questions.0: Which processing stage does Module boundary affect in this exercise? Input cases: [1,2,3] and an invalid file path.
